South Korea will try to cut its reliance on Middle East crude imports to 50% by 2035, Reuters has reported , citing the country’s industry ministry.
The ministry has drafted a 10-year natural resource security plan, which envisages a “fundamental shift” in the way South Korea sources its imports. The plan also calls for a boost in oil reserves by some 20 million barrels by 2030.
South Korea imports as much as 70% of its crude oil from Middle Eastern producers, and most of it must pass through the Strait of Hormuz, the ministry said. The country also imports a lot of gas from the Middle East, although its dependence in gas is much lower, with Middle Eastern imports accounting for a fifth of the total last year. Over the next ten years, South Korea wants to ensure it does not rely on Middle Eastern producers for more than 30% of its gas imports.
